grammar_concept.title: Ellipsis and Substitution
grammar_concept.rule: Avoid repeating a word or phrase already mentioned by omitting it entirely (ellipsis) or replacing it with a short substitute word (one/ones, so, not) — a key feature of natural, non-repetitive English.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: Repeating the exact same words in a reply sounds unnatural and clumsy in English. Instead, native speakers either drop the repeated part completely, or swap it for a small substitute word that carries the same meaning.
grammar_concept.example: I'd like to go, but I can't [go]. — "Will it rain tomorrow?" "I hope not." — "Which shoes do you want?" "The red ones."
grammar_concept.example_translation: Gostava de ir, mas não posso. — "Vai chover amanhã?" "Espero que não." — "Que sapatos queres?" "Os vermelhos."
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: O português tolera mais repetição direta ou resolve isto de outras formas (pronomes clíticos), o que leva a repetir a frase inteira em inglês ("I hope it will not rain" em vez de "I hope not") ou a esquecer substitutos curtos como "one"/"ones" para não repetir um substantivo já mencionado ("Which shoes?" "The red shoes" em vez de "The red ones").
grammar_concept.correction: Depois de um substantivo contável já mencionado, substitua-o por "one"/"ones" em vez de o repetir. Para respostas curtas sobre uma opinião ou expectativa, use "I think so"/"I hope so"/"I hope not"/"I'm afraid not" em vez de repetir a oração inteira.
grammar_concept.real_world_example: In conversation: "Do you think she'll come?" "I hope so."

vocabulary.translation_pt: o/a (substituto de um substantivo já mencionado)
vocabulary.definition_en: used to avoid repeating a countable noun already mentioned
example_sentences: I don't like this shirt — do you have a bigger one?

vocabulary.definition_en: used to say you hope something already mentioned is true, without repeating it
example_sentences: "Will the flight be on time?" "I hope so."

vocabulary.definition_en: a polite way to say no to something already mentioned, without repeating it

exercises.prompt: Complete: "Which shoes do you want?" "The red ___."
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Repetir o substantivo ("the red shoes") em vez de usar "ones" é comum, por transferência do português.

exercises.explanation: "I hope not" substitui toda a oração ("I hope it will not rain") de forma curta e natural.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Responder só "no" (em vez de "I hope not") não erra a gramática, mas perde a estrutura de substituição pedida aqui.

exercises.prompt: What is a polite way to say "no" to a question, without repeating it, like "Is there any left?"?
exercises.explanation: "I'm afraid not" é uma forma educada de dizer "não" sem repetir a pergunta.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. Does the speaker think Sofia will come to the party?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "Do you think Sofia will come?" "I hope so — I really want her to be there."
exercises.transcript: Do you think Sofia will come to the party? I hope so — I really want her to be there.

exercises.prompt: Read: "I wanted to buy the blue jacket, but the shop only had small ones left." What size were the jackets left in the shop?
exercises.explanation: "Small ones" substitui "small jackets" — o tamanho disponível era pequeno.

exercises.prompt: Translate to English (evitando repetir o substantivo): "Não gosto deste casaco, tens um mais quente?"
correct_answer: I don't like this jacket, do you have a warmer one?
exercises.explanation: "One" substitui "jacket" na segunda parte da frase, evitando repeti-lo: "a warmer one".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Repetir "jacket" ("a warmer jacket") em vez de usar "one" é o erro mais comum aqui.

steps.content: Short substitute answers like "I hope so" and "I'm afraid not" usually carry falling intonation at the end, sounding complete and confident despite being so short — not trailing off as if the sentence were unfinished.

steps.prompt: Answer 3 hypothetical questions using short substitutes instead of full repeated sentences — 'I hope so', 'I'm afraid not', 'the [adjective] one(s)'.
Write 3 short exchanges (a question and an answer) that use ellipsis or substitution to avoid repeating a noun or a full clause.
